messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1: rate-limiter-service anomaly — surge of 502/429 for multiple tenants (root cause unknown). Pager: https://pd.example/INC-3123456789

Elise (support): saw the PD page, pinging on-call now. customer impact reports from support for acme-corp.

Owen (on-call SRE): acked on PD. I'm on it — starting collection. Anyone see recent deploys to rate-limiter?

PD Bot: Incident INC-3123456789 acknowledged by Owen (on-call SRE). Escalation level: P1.

Maya (runtime): we had a config push to config-service 4m ago that included a quota-tag mapping change (rollout id: cfg-2026-03-14-09). I didn't think it would be live for global yet, but can check.

Sam (platform): noted. Canary showed no errors but only ~1% traffic. Rolling config to prod 2m ago might have overlapped with limiter rollout.

Owen (on-call SRE): ok runbook steps:
1) confirm limiter health (kubectl, /health)
2) check quota-mapper config and recent commits
3) if misapplied mapping, roll back config or disable enforcement flag
4) open temporary fallback: route non-critical tenants to legacy-limiter

Maya (runtime): running quick checks now.

Maya (runtime): `curl -sS https://rate-limiter.prod.internal/health | jq .` -> `{"status":"ok", "uptime":"3h"}`

Maya (runtime): but `/v1/route?tenant=acme-corp` is returning 502. snippet: ```HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
{"error":"kv-lookup-failed"}```

Owen (on-call SRE): that kv lookup smells like quota-tag mapping. Sam can you check config-service history and whether cfg-2026-03-14-09 flipped a flag?

Sam (platform): checking... `git show --name-only origin/main:configs/quota-mapper.cfg@cfg-2026-03-14-09` -> commits show new mapping table and `enforce_quota_tags=true`.

Sam (platform): also seeing an automated rollout job triggered: `rollout-id=rl-7890` at 09:12 UTC.

Elise (support): customers reporting "requests failing" and "very slow responses". Support ticket count +1 for acme-corp, also 3 other tenants reporting elevated 429s.

Owen (on-call SRE): mitigation plan: disable enforcement flag (hotfix) -> if that stabilizes, then we revert the config roll and re-run canary with stricter checks. Who can flip the flag?

Sam (platform): I can flip it via `kubectl set env deployment/quota-mapper ENFORCE_QUOTA_TAGS=false -n infra` and then roll. Will do in 60s and watch.

Maya (runtime): also prepare fallback route: `route-policy legacy-fallback` to move non-SLA tenants off new path. I'll stage it but not apply until we see effect.

Sam (platform): running: 
```bash
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/quota-mapper ENFORCE_QUOTA_TAGS=false && kubectl rollout restart deployment/quota-mapper -n infra
```

Sam (platform): submitted, rollout started (deployment/quota-mapper). watching pods...

Maya (runtime): metrics: 429 rate for acme-corp peaked at 4.7k/s 2m ago. Total 429s in last 5m: ~18,900. Baseline is ~120/min.

Owen (on-call SRE): oof. estimates: impacting ~0.9% of total requests, but concentrated on high-value tenants — escalate to support/product later.

Sam (platform): rollout status: pods restarted, health checks passing. config process now returning mapping fallback (empty) for mismatched keys.

Maya (runtime): re-testing route: `/v1/route?tenant=acme-corp` -> `200 OK` with token-route `legacy-path`. 429 rate dropping.

Elise (support): customers reporting recovery for acme-corp. they still saw errors for ~7 minutes. logging message from them: "failed requests during checkout window".

Owen (on-call SRE): good. mark as mitigated. still want to confirm root cause: looks like enforce_quota_tags=true caused kv lookup failures when mapping table had an unexpected null key (cfg entry missing). That caused quota-mapper to return error instead of safe-fallback -> cascaded to 502/429.

Maya (runtime): grabbing relevant logs for postmortem: `kubectl logs -l app=quota-mapper --since=10m | grep "null key"` -> shows repeated `panic: missing tag for tenant=acme-corp` entries starting at 09:12:31 UTC.

Sam (platform): opened rollback PR to revert cfg-2026-03-14-09 and added stricter validation to CI: ensure no null tag entries and add canary traffic threshold. PR: https://git.example/repo/PR-2048

Owen (on-call SRE): immediate action items (captured):
- [done] disabled enforce_quota_tags flag -> mitigation success
- [done] restarted quota-mapper pods -> healthy
- [todo] revert config commit (PR-2048) -> Sam
- [todo] add CI validation for mapping files -> Sam
- [todo] postmortem owner + timeline -> Maya/Owen
- [todo] notify affected customers via support -> Elise

Elise (support): I'll prepare customer impact note: affected tenants: acme-corp (severity: high, errors ~7m), beta-shop, flux-tech (intermittent 429s). Draft incoming in #support-updates.

PD Bot: Incident INC-3123456789 status: mitigated. Responder: Owen. Current severity: degraded -> mitigated.

Owen (on-call SRE): will keep thread open for 1h for monitoring, then move to follow-up doc and postmortem. Thanks all for fast responses.

Maya (runtime): logs/alerts archived to incident folder: s3://redwood-incidents/3123456789/

Sam (platform): PR merged to revert config, CI checks added to block null mappings.

Elise (support): customer notes sent. Support will follow up with each tenant tomorrow with timeline and credit as appropriate.

Owen (on-call SRE): closing notes: root cause = config push enabling strict enforcement of quota tags while mapping table contained null entries. Cascade -> kv-lookup errors -> 502/429 spikes. Mitigation = disable enforcement flag + restart quota-mapper.

Owen (on-call SRE): assigning postmortem to Maya. Target draft by EOD tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident INC-3123456789 transitioned to status: resolved (mitigated).
